belongs_to: Cut-out kit page titled 'Number Tokens' (place-value tokens 10,000 / 1,000 / 100 / 10 / 1), after the chapter pages
description: Page with a pink background, the title 'Number Tokens' in script lettering at the top, and a dashed vertical cut line with a scissors icon at its top and bottom running down the LEFT edge. The page holds 87 cut-out tokens, each a rounded rectangle with a dashed black cut outline and its value printed in a dark serif font, arranged in 5 colour bands from top to bottom. Band 1, purple (lilac) tokens '10,000': 9 tokens, row 1 has 5 tokens, row 2 has 4 tokens placed in the gaps between those above (staggered). Band 2, green tokens '1,000': 18 tokens in 4 rows of 5, 4, 5, 4 (every second row staggered). Band 3, orange tokens '100': 20 tokens in 4 rows of 5 (not staggered). Band 4, light-blue tokens '10': 20 tokens in 3 rows of 7, 7, 6 (the third row centred). Band 5, pink tokens '1': 20 tokens in 3 rows of 8, 8, 4 (the third row centred). All tokens are about the same size (roughly 85 x 55 px on the 990 x 1305 page). Footer text 'Reprint 2026-27' at the bottom centre and a faint diagonal watermark across the page (not part of the figure).
unclear: This sheet is part of the book-wide cut-out 'maths figures' kit (pdf pages 13-22); no text of Chapter 15 (pdf pages 1-9) refers to it, so which chapter or question uses it is not known from the book pages.
Token counts (9, 18, 20, 20, 20 = 87) were counted on the picture and match the text layer of the page.

belongs_to: Cut-out kit page headed 'Cut along the dotted lines and fold along the solid lines'; upper figure captioned 'Net of a Icosahedron' (sic)
description: Net of a regular icosahedron made of 20 equal equilateral triangles in a horizontal strip, on a pale cream-green page. Three bands, all fold lines solid and all outer cut lines dotted. Top band: 5 triangles each with its apex pointing UP, standing side by side on the upper solid horizontal line. Middle band: 10 triangles between the two long solid horizontal lines, alternating apex-down and apex-up, the leftmost one apex-down (its left edge is a dotted cut edge) and the rightmost one apex-up; every shared edge inside the strip is a solid fold line. Bottom band: 5 triangles each with its apex pointing DOWN, hanging from the lower solid horizontal line, positioned under the apex-up triangles of the middle band's lower row (shifted half a triangle to the right of the top band). Glue tabs (narrow dotted flaps with a solid fold line along the triangle edge) are drawn on 11 edges: on the right-hand slanted edge of each of the 5 top triangles, on the right-hand slanted edge of the rightmost middle triangle, and on the left-hand slanted edge of each of the 5 bottom triangles. A small scissors icon sits on the dotted tab edge of the first top triangle (start of the cutting line). The caption 'Net of a Icosahedron' is printed centred below the figure.

Triangle count (5 + 10 + 5 = 20) and tab count (5 + 1 + 5 = 11) were counted on a zoomed picture.

belongs_to: Cut-out kit page headed 'Cut along the dotted lines and fold along the solid lines'; lower figure captioned 'Net of a Dodecahedron'
description: Net of a regular dodecahedron made of 12 equal regular pentagons, on a pale cream-green page; fold lines solid, outer cut lines dotted. The net is two 'flowers' of 6 pentagons joined into one piece. Left flower: a central pentagon with its point UP and a flat bottom edge, with one pentagon attached to each of its 5 edges (upper-left, upper-right, left, bottom and right) = 6 pentagons. Right flower: a central pentagon with its point DOWN and a flat top edge, with one pentagon attached to each of its 5 edges (left, top, right, lower-right, lower-left) = 6 pentagons. The two flowers are joined by one shared solid edge: the 'right' pentagon of the left flower is edge-to-edge with the 'left' pentagon of the right flower (that left pentagon sits between the two centres, point UP). Together 12 pentagons. Every outer pentagon edge is dotted (cut), and each outer pentagon also carries a narrow dotted glue flap overlapping one of its edges, with a solid fold line along that edge. A small scissors icon sits on the dotted flap at the top of the upper-left pentagon. The caption 'Net of a Dodecahedron' is printed centred below the figure. The whole net is about 810 px wide and 430 px tall on the 990 x 1305 page, below the icosahedron net.

belongs_to: Kit page of isometric (triangular) dot paper, a blank sheet for drawing; no title or text on the page
description: Blank dot paper on a light-blue page: one thin black rectangle (about 827 x 1150 px on the 990 x 1305 page) filled with small black dots (about 3 px) on a staggered, isometric (triangular) lattice. 50 rows of 31 dots each = 1,550 dots. Neighbouring rows are shifted by half a dot spacing: the top row starts slightly inset from the left border and ends close to the right border, the second row starts closer to the left border and ends further from the right border, and the two patterns alternate down the page. Horizontal dot spacing is about 27 px and the vertical spacing between rows is about 23 px (so the nearest dots form equilateral triangles). No numbers, labels, cut lines or scissors on this page; the footer 'Reprint 2026-27' and a faint diagonal watermark are not part of the figure.
